programme.title: Run
programme.desc: A young man, Jerome, who becomes a cop to find his mother's killer but uncovers dark family secrets, blending personal drama with supernatural/folk horror elements

programme.title: Dunni
programme.desc: About a wealthy man who wanted his only daughter to marry the son of his friend, but his daughter decided not to marry him rather chose to marry one of his father's slave,and suddenly the slave was killed while Dunni ,the only daughter and child of the wealthy man killed herself, reactions as people wanted to know who killed the slave

programme.title: African Bodyguard
programme.desc: Pangaea is a small but wealthy country between Mauritania and the Sahara desert, discover what happened when the First Lady of Pangaea does the unthinkable. The bodyguard will have to protect the palace secret and the future of the country.

programme.title: Concrete Skies
programme.desc: Private detective, WILL MAHONEY, gets the worst news of his life: a diagnosis of stage IV lung cancer with only two months left to live. The bleak prognosis motivates Mahoney to try an untested experimental treatment. With nothing to lose, he vows to take down the drug runners who have eluded him for nine years. Dreary and constantly enshrouded in gray overcast, Syracuse, New York, makes for a highly profitable home base for Bobby and Donnie’s East Coast drug cartel for over a decade. Using connections of his ex-girlfriend, Jennifer, plus his “creative” problem solving skills (ESP), Mahoney infiltrates their inner circle and cripples their operation. Or so it was made to look. Blessed with a remission and a rekindling of his relationship with Jennifer, Mahoney enjoys a blissful vacation with her in Jamaica… only to return to a nightmare worse than terminal cancer! Fists, bullets and deceit fly under the cover of the CONCRETE SKIES!!

programme.title: Mr.Raji
programme.desc: A principal and a deacon, who refuses to change as a child molester and an adulterer, systematically perpetuates his evil deeds.

programme.title: Today is gone
programme.desc: An Interesting Story Of Two Ladies Who Are Best Of Friends And Self Dependant And Hardworking..Namely Rose And Maya. The Lady Rose Suddenly Generated And Had Lust Feelings Towards Maya's Fiancee Namely Bruno. Tho Rose Is In A Serious Relationship with Dave. The Suspense On This Thrilling Movie Tell A Game Challenging Tale Of Mix Feelings On How A Friend Sooner Realised That Her Fiancee Had And Still Have Something With Her Best Friends.

programme.title: The Savages
programme.desc: A sister and brother face the realities of familial responsibility as they begin to care for their ailing father

programme.title: Blood Diamonds
programme.desc: Charles Taylor, then exiled in Nigeria sent a team of mercenaries to Sierra Leone to recover his catch of Diamonds hidden in a coded Cave, but what followed was a mind blowing series of events with the most unexpected outcome.

programme.title: SOREA
programme.desc: Sorea is raped on her way from school. Her family, instead of listening and comforting her, they send her away from home considering her a curse now. She wanders into the unforgiving village, where she has no one else, other than herself. With time, she finds true love, which later turns into another betrayal.

programme.title: Big City Knights
programme.desc: Los Angeles is under attack! Disgruntled ex-government employee, Danks Booth, is bombing government buildings around the country to avenge injustices against him. Set in mid-90's Hollywood, maverick City Marshal Jack Dalton, recently "reassigned" to the LA city marshals division due to their lack of appreciation for his irrepressible nature, recognized the destruction as Danks' handi work.

programme.title: The Millions Men
programme.desc: Can the team of con artists find a way to convince Emmanuel Afolabi, to part with the required fifty percent for the LPO? How would they beat the binary encryption to authenticate their product without getting caught or even killed?

programme.title: Irinajo
programme.desc: Based on parental trust a young lady traveled to Cairo in Egypt to work and was sending money to her father to build a house for her not knowing the Father was only using the money for himself,after two years,she came home and found out no one can be trust even her father

programme.title: Stolen Rose
programme.desc: Stand out is a high school sports movie about Medi a passionate footballer who bribes to get a bursary on a school team but it lasts until a new coach arrives. Now he must convince the new coach to keep him on the team and prevent his mum from finding out

programme.title: Red Paws
programme.desc: After their parents die, Bolce Nekesa ( VICTORIA NAYA ) is left with the responsibility to take care of her sister. She gets a job with an international human trafficking criminal, which suits her financial needs quit well. Now Interpol sends their rough agent Brandon Williams ( JOHN KING ) to track the bunch down. The ghettos become warfield. Will Bolce remain standing?

programme.title: Nwanyi Bu Ife 1
programme.desc: A Father abandons his girl children immediately he realised that he had a male child with another woman. This breaks the family apart but 4th e children receive determined to prove to their father that a girl child is as valuable too.

programme.title: Nwanyi Bu Ife 2
programme.desc: A Father abandons his girl children immediately he realised that he had a male child with another woman. This breaks the family apart but 4th e children receive determined to prove to their father that a girl child is as valuable too.

programme.title: In The Wooden Box
programme.desc: Frank, a charity Organisation manager finds himself locked up in a wooden box. The only thing he has is a mobile phone, with no service and no signal network. Mixed with love, this claustrophobic thriller will leave you breathless.

programme.title: Edima
programme.desc: Edima and Ogechi using their NYSC for prostitution as things get twisted, Edima refuse to continue with the life, but Ogechi decides to set Edima up as she refuse to continue in the business.

programme.title: The challenge
programme.desc: Patrick Reilly, a mid-life street fighter (Tim Scanlon) and former golden gloves champ, is approached by a boxing trainer who asks him to come back to the gym and train for the pro boxing circuit. Reilly considers the chance to make a comeback. At home Reilly's girl, Tammie, finds that she is in love with a time bomb who can only function by winning. Once at the gym he runs into Ray Rinaldi's grandson, a Pro boxer, and they clash after Reilly sees his manager prompting a situation between the two fighters. But when tempers flare and challenges are made Reilly resorts to what he knows best, finding his opponent's weakness.

programme.title: Awadia
programme.desc: The lustfulness of the king over the daughter of AWADIA throw the entire kingdom into a great disarray until the adventure of seven (7) virgins into the evil forest in other to safe the kingdom from mysterious death

programme.title: Enclosed
programme.desc: Three freinds with different phases of mariage, and regardless of their freinship status, their marriages faced different reactions base on each man's approach to his mariage.

programme.title: Ajo onye isi
programme.desc: A rich man who killed his servant to marry his wife

programme.title: Osuru
programme.desc: Osuru plunges you into the heart of ancestral traditions and power struggles within an African kingdom.

programme.title: Anorah's Novella
programme.desc: Your purpose in life can never be voided even through the odd of life as this journey will take you to an existing Insane Girl who happens to be the solution to the entire people in the land even in her insane state, She was chase to be kill, Love by a man, War in the land and solution in the land.

programme.title: Iju Uwa (The Journey of life Part 1)
programme.desc: The short story details the suffering of a young man whose destiny was damaged by his late father.

programme.title: Okomfo Anokye Poma
programme.desc: A Man Dies And Wills All His Properties To His Son, But The Will Also States That, His Son Can Only Inherit The Properties Unless He Goes Back To His Hometown To Fight And Bring The STAFF OF The Legendary OKOMFO ANOKYE. What Is His Reason And What Is The Connection Between This Man And The Historical High Priest OKOMFO ANOKYE?*

programme.title: Madam Sidechick
programme.desc: Deji and Miranda has long time relationship before he met his sidechick. The reaction of Miranda was not funny when she discovered Chioma her man's sidechick

programme.title: Return Of Black Monkey
programme.desc: This story deals with aspects of the European Colonization of the African continent in a very simple but unique way. The story also suggests that, both the Black Man and the White Man worship the same Almighty God but through different mediums.

programme.title: Reynolds City
programme.desc: Tracer, a hit man with emotional issues, is on a job to collect from a client when it goes sour. Shaken by the experience, he vows to do one last job so that he can be the kind of father his young son has always craved. Katherine Macro, a beautiful independent newswoman, pays for a disc of the Mayor raping a female staffer. What she doesn’t know is the Mayor and Carlo; his security guard with a dangerously violent personality, have hired Tracer to kill her before she can run the story. She gets a call from her friend Gage Johnson; a former cop turned no nonsense hit man.

programme.title: I Pray For Love
programme.desc: Obiora and Chioma are two love birds in the village until Amaka made her to Obiora.

programme.title: Broken Crayon
programme.desc: The Lives of two sisters, a recalcitrant and a compliant revolves round selfish family members in three tales of violence, redemption and regret.

programme.title: Trip To Libya
programme.desc: Some girls in their desperation to travel abroad to make it quick together with Franca whom out of poverty and impatient dropped out of school, found themselves in the hand of Mr shortcut who led them to human trafficker Don Bruce, but halfway taking them to slavery in attempt to expose the link of the local Mafia to the foreign prostitution ring , as Ragler tries to save the girls, officer Ben paid the ultimate price.

programme.title: Polio and Politics
programme.desc: Polio and Politics is centered on polio eradication in Africa. The need for an artistic intervention through the film medium which is more popular than stage and radio in Africa, has become very necessary. Aware that the WHO's goals centered on eradication of polio, malaria and several other diseases plaguing the continent of Africa. programme.title: Crave
programme.desc: Warning: do not watch Crave on an empty stomach. Because we’ll have you craving a creamy scoop of ice cream bedded on a crispy waffle. Or really, really needing to crunch into juicy fried chicken right now. Hosted by Charlotte Mei, the runner-up of Eat List Star, Crave finds out what gets celebrities salivating – roti prata, roast meats, sushi, satay, salted egg ice cream, buah keluak, and even an English-style big breakfast! Our celebrities’ cravings know no bounds, and anything from local to Japanese to Mediterranean fare is fair game – as long as they crave it. And there’s a little special by Charlotte. On every show, she will cook a dish – guaranteed to make you crave for it!

They sign their wedding vows. Months later, Astrid, stressed, wants a child to secure her fortune. Ezequiel, without results, wants to make Camila fall in love.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Anton takes Ezequiel kidnapped and warns Fausto, so that he can have the pleasure of killing him. Under deception they summon Amelia and Sebastian to make Fausto reason with them to free Ezequiel, otherwise she and her unborn child will die.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Ezequiel and Fausto, at loggerheads. Camila tries to convince Roger to release Ezequiel. The situation is complicated because Amelia, held hostage and accompanied by Sebastian, is already in labor.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Sebastian, dodging Anton's shots, takes Amelia to the hospital. There, their baby is born. Fausto takes Ezequiel again as his hostage. Fausto and Patricia are thrilled to meet their grandson and Amelia asks her father to honor his word to let Ezequiel go free.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Ezequiel feels betrayed and hands over his daughter to the infamous Celso who intends to abuse her. Sebastian saves her from the incident. Camila, sad, continues with her plan to destroy the life of her godmother Elda and tells Ezequiel her reason for doing so: the betrayal of her mother, accusing her unjustly.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Patricia is terrified because Celso wants to kill her son Gregorio. Fausto, annoyed, orders to keep an eye on her. Elda, who receives flowers from Alfredo, fears that Luciano will discover her.

programme.title: Five Finger Death Punch interview - Zoltan Bathory
programme.desc: Zoltan about being forced to take a break, what drives him, living life to the fullest, manifesting thoughts, wanting to be an astronaut, getting started on AfterLife, the band being polarizing, success and envy, fresh energy in the band, true creative freedom, the concept of AfterLife, a cultural paradigm shift, near-death experiences, spirituality, Judgement Day.

programme.title: Big Thief interview - Adrienne Lenker
programme.desc: Adrianne about curiosity, a sense of stillness, creativity and songwriting, music as a bridge to the etherial world, tapping into inspiration, why we do what we do, starting on the new album U.F.O.F, dealing with success, keeping a connection with yourself as you evolve, wanting to be part of something bigger, how the band was formed, the album title, alienation in society, sharing her art.

programme.title: Daughtry interview - Chris Daughtry
programme.desc: Chris about Heavy Is The Crown, the most liberating album he’s made, starting again from the ground up, going independent, the writing process for World On Fire, challenging himself vocally, finding his voice, Chris Cornell and covering ‘Hunger Strike’, going sober, mental health, dealing with his struggles through song.

programme.title: Death Angel interview - Ted Aguilar
programme.desc: Ted about being a Death Angel fan from day 1, coming up in the Bay Area trash scene, how he got into music, joining Death Angel, his first shows with the band, perseverance and the love for playing music, The Bastard Tracks, his favorite live tracks, rare live tracks, the challenges with Frolic Through the Park, acoustic songs, his thoughts on Rob and Mark’s lyrics, Tom Petty, working on a new Death Angel album, not being able to tour, adapting to a changing industry.

programme.title: Sleaford Mods with jason Part 1
programme.desc: Jason about Teacher Faces Porn Charges, starting on the album English Tapas, current affairs, a hip hop influence, getting the working class tag, humor, self-reflection, Messy Anywhere, Andrew’s beats, getting critiqued, people’s opinions, the temperament of English people, Rough Trade, their music abroad, the live shows, genuine elation, having no pretense, professionalism

programme.title: Marlon Williams interview
programme.desc: Marlon about touring with Lorde, dabbling in acting, the start of My Boy, being judged publicly, eclectic songwriting, the song My Boy, simplicity in his writing, Māori strumming, Don’t Go Back, finding a healthy work/life balance, Thinking of Nina, Soft Boys Make The Grade

programme.title: Bastille interview - Dan Smith
programme.desc: Dan about the new album Give Me The Future, his modes of escaping the world, seeing Big Thief live, their music being about escapism, his style of songwriting, being more certain in what he wants to say, using sci-fi to tell stories with substance, Future Holds, a poem by Riz Ahmed, how we perceive the future, creating a fictional world for the album, songwriting as an escape, learning to be a frontman, how he feels on stage, having a #1 album again, what’s next for the band.

programme.title: David Paich interview
programme.desc: David about writing poems as a child, Elton John, Houston I’m Coming To See You, forming Toto, Hold The Line, Rosanna, track splicing and modern production, working on The Girl Is Mine, Forgotten Toys, Queen Charade, Forward, Willibelongtoyou, Spirit of the Moonrise, All The Tears That Shine

programme.title: Alt-J interview - Thom Sonny Green
programme.desc: Thom about taking a year off, getting ready for The Dream, Walk a Mile, having no expectations for the new album, channeling his feelings into music, Shakespeare, his passion for art, Philadelphia, their growing friendship within the band, Get Better, field recordings and playing with sound, thinking about another solo album.

programme.title: Jinjer interview - Tatiana and Eugene
programme.desc: Tatiana and Eugene rising in popularity, releasing the new album Wallflowers, adjust to life without touring, music as escapism, the writing process, working on the sound of the new album, Tatiana needing pressure to write lyrics, being a live-oriented band, high-flowing poetry, improvising with vocals, personal lyrics, Copycat and authenticity in art, creating something of your own

programme.title: Steven Wilson interview
programme.desc: Steven about releasing an album during the pandemic, falling out of love with the guitar, the origins of his new album The Future Bites, living in an electronic world, Eddie van Halen, King Ghost, an exciting songwriting process, making the characters he writes about believable, creativity and technology, the internet changing human nature, the decline of truth and reality, positive change, the year 2032 an consumer culture, curiosity being under threat.

programme.title: Tom Chaplin interview
programme.desc: Tom about climate change, a new attitude to living, parenthood and growing older, asking yourself the difficult questions, happiness not being a destination, not fitting in as a teenager and dealing with negative emotions, Stars Align and working with Ethan Johns, electronic sounds, Gonna Run, brutally honest lyrics, the road he has traveled, Overshoot

programme.title: Damien Jurado Interview
programme.desc: Damien about how his songs come to him, Bird Tricked Into The Tree, not overthinking music, an emphasis on his vocals, producing without friend Richard Swift, his inner voice, Ochoa, the album title What’s New, Tomboy?, the characters he writes about, artists vs entertainers, connecting through music, Oh Yeah by Bo Diddley.

programme.title: Destroyer interview - Dan Bejar
programme.desc: Dan about film scores, when he became obsessed with songwriting, instrumental music, using the original vocal tapes, Crimson Tide, lyrics and sounds, The Television Music Supervisor, a collective process, Cue Synthesizer, his musical identity, figuring out how to play the record live, the title Have We Met.

programme.title: Bob Mould interview
programme.desc: Bob about his early fascination with music, songs he wrote when he was 9, discovering punk rock, The Ramones and Iggy Pop, forming Hüsker Dü, gaining attention, when the band fell apart, Workbook, his time in Sugar, his parents passing, moving to Berlin, writing for Sunshine Rock.

programme.title: St. Vincent interview
programme.desc: Annie about how she started in music, creative expression, the sound of the early 70s, writing for her new album Daddy’s Home, writing about flawed people, Somebody Like Me, finding stillness for the first time, not worrying about the commercial side, signing an autograph in prison, why she decided to write about the incarceration of her father, the Wurlitzer, working with Jack Antonoff, the various ways of writing songs, knowing when a song is done, performing at SNL.

programme.title: Cindy Blackman interview
programme.desc: Cindy about The Quarantine Blues, a chance to reset, becoming better humans, her love for the drums, always looking to improve, singing a lot on the new album Give The Drummer Some, We Came To Play, Mother Earth, sharing music, bringing jazz to more people, not putting music into boxes, inspiration, the incredible jazz musicians she learned from, enjoying the little things.

programme.title: Jean-Michel Jarre interview
programme.desc: Jean-Michel about Welcome To The Other Side, a virtual Notre Dame, the impact of the pandemic on music, innovations in music technology, binaural recording, VR and augmented reality as new forms of expression, the value of music, respecting intellectual property, this being only the beginning of the digital age, artificial intelligence, Ray Charles and Pierre Soulages, lessons from his mother, a street in Lyon being named after his mother

programme.title: Countain Crows interview - Adam Duritz
programme.desc: Adam about visiting his friends farm in England, shaving his head, starting on the Butter Miracle EP, music being a personal thing for him, Tall Grass, the evolution of his songwriting, the ghosts from your childhood, learning how to live, a screw-up with the release, working on a second Butter Miracle suite, keeping true to the song, a trumpet solo, the album getting so much support, feeling responsible for his crew.

programme.title: Between The Buried And Me interview - Dustie Waring
programme.desc: Dustie about his mindset around the first Colors album, never repeating themselves, songs that are difficult to play, pushing themselves, working on Colors II during the pandemic, writing the album over the internet, a collective writing approach, believing in albums, being proud of what you create, preparing for live shows, art that takes risks, creative freedom, bands that last.

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about his album Zeros, finding his place in music, playfulness, making observations about society, a positive sense of humanity, Daniel You’re Still a Child, The Social Dilemma documentary, turning off his notifications, the good and bad of social media, organic and raw sounds, good mistakes, capturing the right energy on the album, trusting yourself as a musician, taking control, finally getting the album out, his favorite lyric on the album.

programme.title: Glass Animals interview - Joe Seaward
programme.desc: Joe about gearing up towards the third album Dreamland, suffering a terrible accident, a time for reflection, not taking things for granted, finding out who the people around you really are, the first rehearsal after the accident, the songwriting for Dreamland, Your Love, how he connects with all of the songs on the album, songs that make you feel, not being able to tour the album, finding new ways to present the album.

programme.title: Sleaford Mods with jason Part 2
programme.desc: Jason about Teacher Faces Porn Charges, starting on the album English Tapas, current affairs, a hip hop influence, getting the working class tag, humor, self-reflection, Messy Anywhere, Andrew’s beats, getting critiqued, people’s opinions, the temperament of English people, Rough Trade, their music abroad, the live shows, genuine elation, having no pretense, professionalism

programme.title: DMA's interview - Tommy O'Dell
programme.desc: Tommy about their show at the Brixton Academy and Liam Gallagher, finding his voice, the album Glow, dance elements, writing lyrics, Silver, staying true to yourself, ambition, not trying to please everyone, Never Before, Criminals and pop, songs that evolve on the road, Life is a Game of Changing, what he learned as a frontman.

programme.title: Kevin Morby interview
programme.desc: Kevin about religion, the song Beautiful Strangers, the phrase “Oh My God”, showing religion from all angles, growing up in the midwest, working with Sam Cohen again, his vocals, writing on airplanes, Hail Mary, unconventional songs, talking his time with the album, a therapeutic element, the song OMG.

programme.title: Katie Melua interview
programme.desc: Katie about her new album No. 8, playing the entire album live, Remind Me To Forget, her first studio album without Mike Batt, changing things up, celebrating great musicianship, working with producer Leo Abrahams, developing as a songwriter, English Manner, her divorce, love propaganda, focusing on what’s important, being adventurous, getting into photography.

programme.title: Armin van Buuren
programme.desc: Armin about always wanting his own radio show, the growth of EDM, having his own radio studio, listening to colleagues, psytrance, ‘Great Spirit’ with Vini Vici, the format for A State of Trance, the 800th episode, dreams for the future, Armin Only in the Amsterdam Arena

programme.title: Joe Satriani interview
programme.desc: Joe about when he was still a beginner on guitar, working hard to get better, NYC in the early 70s, the surrealness of his career, teaching Steve Vai, finding “work-arounds” as a guitar player, Eddie van Halen, The Elephants of Mars, experimentation, composing songs over the internet, songs coming together organically, a song inspired by Questlove, Randy Rhoads and what keeps inspiring him.

programme.title: Jack Savoretti interview
programme.desc: Jack about his new album Europiana, nostalgia about his childhood holidays, an education in music, finding a purpose behind what he does, scoring his second number one album, surrounding himself with the right people, writing on piano, the impact of the lockdown, working with Nile Rodgers, loving the notion of a full album, recording at Abbey Road and the magic in that studio, asking questions about true love.

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about political engagement, making people think, The Kids Don’t Wanna Come Home, confusion, younger generations, his first songs, rowdy live shows, winning over crowds, a sold-out tour, his upcoming debut record, growing as a songwriter

programme.title: Eefje de Visser interview
programme.desc: Eefje over haar nieuwe plaat Bitterzoet, muziek voor in de auto, schrijven vanuit piano, haar thuisstudio, niet te braaf willen zijn, een internationaal gevoel, altijd beginnen bij de muziek, kritisch zijn op haar eigen teksten, beeldvorming, tegenstellingen, vluchten uit de realiteit, verloren potentie, zelf-bewustzijn, vol inspiratie zitten.

programme.title: DMA's interview - Johnny Took
programme.desc: Johnny about the past 2 years, their loyal fans, early influences and genre-blending, the evolution of their sound, having loads of time in the studio, shaping How Many Dreams?, I Don’t Need To Hide, creating a dynamic live show, old vs new songs, De Carle and pushing boundaries

programme.title: HMLTD interview - Henry Spychaliski and Achilleas Sarantaris
programme.desc: Henry and Achilleas about memories of a good time in Amsterdam, being commodified, Loaded, wanting to make a cultural impact, getting dropped by Sony, a duty to the album, banding together, West of Eden, painting a picture of the world, music as celebration, immersive live shows, challenging the audience, imagination, a period of reflection.

programme.title: Band of Horses interview - Ben Bridwell
programme.desc: Ben about needing a change, taking a stab at producing the album, the sound of Things Are Great, making a connection, sounding more like himself, Warning Signs, having success, struggling during lockdown, his love for songwriting, being a conduit for songs, being a fan of music first, trusting himself.

programme.title: Larkin Poe_interview
programme.desc: Rebecca and Megan about playing for change, the power of music, unlearning some of their musical upbringing, trusting themselves, forging their own path, five years of growth, going to Nashville to record Blood Harmony, the art of pre-production, sibling harmonies, still surprising each other, ambition

programme.title: Myles Kennedy interview
programme.desc: Myles about a road trip through America, getting out of your bubble, his new solo album The Ides of March, slide guitar, the Sifting Through The Fire intro, making sense of the world and songwriting, Get Along, playing the blues, Love Rain Down, the title track, uncertainty about the future, affecting people with music, the need to create, and a lot more! (11/05/2021)

programme.title: Blind Melon interview - Rogers Stevens and Christopher Thorn
programme.desc: Rogers and Christopher the early years of the band, realizing their dreams, Shannon Hoon filming the band all the time, the documentary All I Can Say, watching the footage for the first time, who they were back then, the night Shannon died, bittersweet moments, what kind of person Shannon was, how his mom reacted to the film, Change and Shannon’s voice, the randomness of life, how they handled Shannon’s death.

programme.title: Agnes Obel interview
programme.desc: Agnes about playing piano at an early age, starting to write her own songs, lyrics. and melodies, tapping into the stream of inspiration, a great sense of freedom, Myopia, Camera’s Rolling, playing with pitch, knowing when you’re on the right track, experimenting with her voice, vocals vs instrumentals

programme.title: P.J. Morton interview
programme.desc: P.J. about the music he grew up with, the first song he ever wrote, his early career and learning about the industry, delving into production, his sound, digging deeper on Watch The Sun, his computer crashing, how the lockdowns influenced the album, Be Like Water, working with Nas and Stevie Wonder, Please Don’t Walk Away, catharsis through songwriting

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: 2026 BRICS SUMMIT | New Blueprint of the Global South
programme.desc: The 2026 BRICS Summit takes place on 12-13 September in New Delhi, India. Assembling a distinguished group of senior Chinese and Indian scholars and experts, CGTN Biztalk joins with WION from India launching a special episode of TV panel discussion, to find out how expanded BRICS representation translate into deeper cooperation and a more influential role in global governance.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: Sky's The Limit
programme.desc: A documentary exploring the muralist movement: the art of painting over breathtaking heights. Windowless gable walls were graffiti painters’ early targets, particularly in urban areas under renovation, and since 2012, monumental graffiti is in full rebirth especially in Paris’ 13th arrondissement. Through a design thought as a décor, obliterating the blandness of the walls, artists skillfully revive these soulless surfaces.

programme.title: The Rivers
programme.desc: Mai Hua, French-Vietnamese single mom with two children, brings back her dying grandmother to France. programme.title: Dances with the Wind
programme.desc: ‘Fury Dance’ is a story about a Korean protest dancer, Sam-hun Lee. He fought for the democratization of South Korea in the ‘80’s through dance, while giving up his own dream to become a ballerino. The film takes the viewer through prominent events in South Korean history, as Sam-hun dances to soothe the souls of victims who were killed by the Korean national violence during the past 30 years. During the 1980 Gwangju Massacre however, Sam-hun developed a panic disorder. So he crosses through the Eurasian rail with difficulty when invited to attend a festival to dance in France. Through his journey, he attempts to overcome his claustrophobic fears in France, revisits his lost dream of becoming a ballerino in Russia, and dances for the Holocaust victims in Poland. Documented for 15 years, this film is dedicated to those who lost their noble lives while fighting for freedom against the unjust political power.

programme.desc: Neil who is a painter and graphic designer, on a morning just like any other morning his girlfriend Amanda leaves him and moves out of their house (don't worry, it's a rental.) That morning Neil tries to cope as best he knows how, but in a strange turn of events he ends up shooting back a glass of bleach. He wakes up to suicide watch and court appointed therapy as well as the empty void Amanda left. Now Neil has to decide what he can do to feel better about himself. Should he get Amanda back? Make his old friends like him again? Confront his estranged father? Eat a ton of Chinese food? Or maybe he should just finish his latest goddamned painting.

Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Miriam de Paoli: romper tabúes sobre la menopausia con No Pausa.
programme.desc: "La menopausia no es una enfermedad. Es una etapa natural de nuestras vidas." En este nuevo episodio de Fundadoras, Sabrina Díaz Ibarra conversa con Miriam de Paoli, fundadora de No Pausa, periodista, innovadora social y referente en longevidad y salud femenina. ¿Qué pasa cuando una mujer tarda más de un año en recibir un diagnóstico para una etapa natural como el climaterio? ¿Por qué seguimos en silencio sobre la menopausia? ¿Cómo pueden la tecnología, los datos y la comunidad cambiarlo todo? Una charla poderosa sobre romper tabúes, emprender con propósito y construir un futuro más inclusivo para las mujeres. Suscribite al canal y activá la campanita para más entrevistas con mujeres que están transformando el mundo. Encontranos también en Instagram y LinkedIn como @sabrinadiazibarra #Fundadoras #NoPausa #MiriamDePaoli #Menopausia #SaludFemenina #Longevidad #Climaterio #InnovaciónSocial

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Entrevista a Helena Estrada
programme.desc: En esta conversación, Helena Estrada nos comparte su visión sobre el liderazgo femenino, la independencia financiera y el poder de tomar las riendas de nuestra vida. Con una trayectoria que abarca el derecho, las finanzas y el coaching, nos deja reflexiones profundas sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que enfrentamos las mujeres hoy. "Estamos tan educadas en querer ser queridas..." "Un costo siempre pagamos... la pregunta es cuál es mayor en tu vida, si ser una persona o ser personaje. Y acá no hay muchos grises." Además, nos habla sobre su más reciente libro, El viaje de la heroína (2025), y su compromiso con generar cambios reales. Mirá la entrevista completa y dejate inspirar.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Eli Bracciaforte: De Workana a No Pausa, liderazgo y proyectos inspiradores
programme.desc: En esta entrevista, Eliana Bracciaforte comparte su experiencia como fundadora de Workana y No Pausa, reflexiona sobre los retos de emprender desde cero, y revela cómo impulsa el crecimiento de mujeres en un mundo profesional en constante cambio. Un diálogo inspirador sobre liderazgo, aprendizajes y su compromiso con transformar la menopausia en un tema clave para el bienestar femenino.

programme.title: Afrontar la adolescencia de tus hijos, Duelo emocional de las madre, Momento de DESmadre Podcast
programme.desc: En este episodio de Momento de DESmadre, conversamos con la terapeuta familiar Erika Ángulo sobre uno de los temas más desafiantes para muchas madres: la adolescencia de los hijos y el duelo emocional que sentimos al verlos crecer y empezar a soltarse de nuestra mano. Hablamos sobre cómo manejar la etapa de la "aborrecencia", entender los cambios emocionales y de comportamiento de los adolescentes, y cómo las mamás podemos vivir este proceso sin tanta culpa, con herramientas que nos ayuden a conectar desde el amor y la empatía. Temas que tocamos: Cómo lidiar con la adolescencia de los hijos Qué es el duelo emocional en la maternidad Cambios emocionales en los adolescentes Cómo soltar y dejar crecer a los hijos sin dolor Consejos de una terapeuta familiar para madres Escucha, comparte y acompáñanos en este momento de reflexión y desahogo maternal. ¡No estás sola! Suscríbete para más conversaciones reales, sin filtros y con mucho DESmadre. #Adolescencia #MaternidadReal #PodcastParaMujeres #DueloMaternal #MomentoDeDESmadre #ErikaÁngulo #Adolescentes #Familia #PodcastEnEspañol

programme.title: MINISTERIO DE BRUJAS: Carta Astral de Los Javis, Caras de Bélmez, Mal de Ojo y Venus en Escorpio.
programme.desc: Bienvenid@s al Ministerio de Brujas, el único programa donde la magia tiene reglamento, las dudas tienen expediente y la intuición legisla sin oposición. En este episodio, grabado en vivo en@CanalBarro el aquelarre vino encendido. PROTOCOLO DE LA HOGUERA Quemamos todo lo que necesita transformarse: los crush imposibles de tu ideología opuesta, la gente que vive diciendo “no”, los silencios incómodos del WhatsApp y esa tortura mental llamada “debería estar haciendo algo”. Aquí el fuego purifica… o al menos nos da permiso para reírnos. SECRETARÍA DE VENUS EN TANGA Nos adentramos en el magnetismo oscuro de Venus en Escorpio: deseo extremo, intensidad emocional, tabúes, renacer afectivo y ese erotismo que ve en la piel ajena un archivo confidencial. Además, tiramos una carta del tarot erótico para leer el clima del deseo. DIRECCIÓN GENERAL DE CINEMATOGRAFÍA ZODIAZAL La Dra. Fernanda Garrido trae cine, signos y elementos. Películas que dialogan con el cielo y con nuestras crisis de identidad astrológica. Cine como brújula, literal. programme.title: Unrolled

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Rick Rodriguez West Tampa Tobacco Co
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Rick Rodriguez, also known as "Chef Rick," from West Tampa Tobacco, who explains his nickname comes from blending tobacco like a chef uses food to create a desired flavor profile. Rick introduces new cigars like the "Circle of Life," a tribute to his mentors, and the "Double Crab," part of a Tampa-inspired trilogy, shaped like a "flying pig". He shares his personal journey into the cigar industry at age 40 and emphasizes that for him, cigars represent "connection" and a "gateway for a new friendship".

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Brian Motola And George Hadweh Cavalier
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Brian and George from Cavalier Cigars, who discuss their roles within the company, with Brian as a partner in the Honduran factory (FBT) and George as the sales representative for Florida and Puerto Rico. programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people’s southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 1
programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. From its Porcelain Tower - one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, to its grand city walls and ancient palaces, join us on a voyage across time to experience the echoes of history in Nanjing's storied bricks.

programme.title: Chengde, Where Emperors Escaped to
programme.desc: Chengde is a prefecture-level city in Hebei Province, bordering northeast Beijing and dubbed Beijing’s backyard. Including three parts, this episode features Chengde’s temples, Longhua’s hot springs and Xinglong’s mountains, highlighting the city’s history and abundant natural resources.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World
programme.desc: When people hear "Spring Festival," they often think of fireworks, red lanterns, and lion dances in the streets. But today, these traditions have grown beyond merely a once-a-year celebration, weaving themselves into people's daily lives across China. The documentary "Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World" embarks on a cultural journey across the nation, tracing how ancient Chinese traditions continue to evolve and engage people worldwide.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.4
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.4
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.1
programme.desc: When Zhejiang's winding river meets the sea it encounters a coastal region studded with islands. On this journey we survey a land of bays, bridges and harbors that is a glorious archipelago of memory, history and culture...

programme.title: Shunde's flavors: where tradition blends with vivid daily life
programme.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures – from crispy fish skin to fried milk – into culinary wonders. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia, are setting out to taste the flavors and feel the warmth of Shunde's countryside with the locals.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing's merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 1 - From Relic to Resort
programme.desc: The first episode of the Hotel Series introduces three hotels reconstructed from ancient buildings , each of the hotels has its unique stunning style: 1. Yingui Boutique Hotel reconstructed from ancient buildings with traditional Bai ethnic minority style in Kunming, Yunnan; 2. Imperial Guard Boutique Hotel reconstructed from Anhui Huangshan Huipai architecture; 3. Yellow River Suji Hotel Group in Shapotou, Zhongwei, Ningxia. This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art
programme.desc: The documentary "Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art" follows a heritage master and a visionary show director as they carry a thousand-year-old craft into the future. Originating in Liuyang City, Hunan Province, Liuyang fireworks have evolved from ritual folk traditions into a modern art form that integrates cutting-edge technology. Check out how Liuyang fireworks paint stories across the sky.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.5
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.5
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.2
programme.desc: Sichuan's western mountains are a shield safeguarding a true national treasure: the Chengdu Plain, China's very own land of plenty. Join us as we dive from high plateaus into deep gorges, scale snow peaks, and follow rivers in pursuit of an engineering marvel bequeathed by the ancients...

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing's merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 1 - From Relic to Resort
programme.desc: The first episode of the Hotel Series introduces three hotels reconstructed from ancient buildings , each of the hotels has its unique stunning style: 1. Yingui Boutique Hotel reconstructed from ancient buildings with traditional Bai ethnic minority style in Kunming, Yunnan; 2. Imperial Guard Boutique Hotel reconstructed from Anhui Huangshan Huipai architecture; 3. Yellow River Suji Hotel Group in Shapotou, Zhongwei, Ningxia. This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art
programme.desc: The documentary "Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art" follows a heritage master and a visionary show director as they carry a thousand-year-old craft into the future. Originating in Liuyang City, Hunan Province, Liuyang fireworks have evolved from ritual folk traditions into a modern art form that integrates cutting-edge technology. Check out how Liuyang fireworks paint stories across the sky.

programme.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.5
programme.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.5
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.2
programme.desc: Sichuan's western mountains are a shield safeguarding a true national treasure: the Chengdu Plain, China's very own land of plenty. Join us as we dive from high plateaus into deep gorges, scale snow peaks, and follow rivers in pursuit of an engineering marvel bequeathed by the ancients...

programme.title: Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programme.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama – they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.

programme.title: Foodwise: Changsha
programme.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May embark on a journey to Changsha in Hunan Province.?They taste their way through the local cuisine, discover the city's latest art and fashion trends, and find out why this place is one of China's "influencer hotspots", attracting millions of domestic and foreign tourists each year.

programme.title: Foodwise: Qingdao
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: White Crane
programme.desc: In Yongchun, China, Kleber explores the origins of White Crane kungfu and its effect on the martial arts world. He learns how its blocks and strikes were inspired by animal movements, and how acupuncture points can be used to deadly effect. After training his grip and finger strength with wooden sticks, he travels to Beijing for an introduction to Goju-ryu karate, and discovers striking similarities with White Crane.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 3
programme.desc: Join us in Nanjing's bustling old quarter, where you can try on silk dresses worth their weight in gold, and see how traditional handicrafts have been given modern twists. We'll feast on street snacks and local delicacies by the old Confucian Temple, before taking a pleasure cruise along Nanjing's mother river to round off our exploration of this vibrant and historic city.

programme.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 2 - Designing Hotels
programme.desc: The second episode of the Hotel Series features three uniquely styled design hotels: the industrial-style Zhagen Shanyu Hotel in Chongqing, Yisheng Hotel in Wuxi, Jiangsu, and the Naxi-style Shujia Yulu Boutique Hotel in Lijiang, Yunnan. This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Sculpting the Soul of Tianjin
programme.desc: Let's journey into the soul of Tianjin through the story of Zhang Yu – the sixth-generation inheritor of the famed Clay Figure Zhang family. As part of the documentary series "Next Stop: China," this episode reveals how one man's dedication bridges centuries of artistry with the pulse of a modern metropolis.

programme.title: In Search of Shunde Ep.1
programme.desc: A Bite of Shunde tells the stories of Shunde locals through food, showcasing this city’s heritage and present-day life. It looks at the craftsmanship Shunde people apply in the kitchen and beyond, and the dedicated, artisan mentality behind their renowned culinary culture. Through their attitude toward a simple home-cooked meal, we get insights into their values and way of life.

programme.title: Blossom China
programme.desc: Every year when the flowers come into full bloom, countless people across China set out for the country’s most popular flower-viewing destinations to enjoy nature’s colorful spectacle, fueling an increasingly vibrant "flower-tourism" economy. What ecological progress has made this possible, and how is it reshaping local communities? In the 30-minute CGTN special Blossom China, host Liu Qiuyuan, reporter Idah, and host Martin visit the “Train to Spring” at Juyongguan in Beijing, the peony-filled China National Flower Garden and Longmen Grottoes in Luoyang, and the breathtaking Baili Azalea Scenic Area in Bijie, Guizhou—sharing the stories behind the blossoms through a unique lens.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.3
programme.desc: Inner Mongolia spans China from east to west. Little wonder then, that it's such a land of diversity - epic landscapes of forests, grasslands and deserts, Inner Mongolia has it all!

programme.title: The secret of the 'Long Hair' village
programme.desc: For the Red Yao women of Guangxi, southern China, hair is far more than a mark of beauty – it's a living narrative of identity, lineage, and nature. Each stage of life is reflected in how they wear it, carrying the memory of their families and the wisdom of their ancestors. Their time-honored rice-water hair care ritual is not just a beauty secret – it's a thread connecting generations, preserving ecological knowledge passed down through centuries. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they step into Huangluo Yao Village, known as the "World's Longest Hair Village," to uncover the stories and traditions behind the Red Yao's legendary long hair.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan’s explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of “opening the gate”, the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou’s rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. programme.title: Foodwise: Quanzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in Quanzhou, the ancient starting point of the Maritime Silk Road. From its covered arcades and Roman columns to its Southeast Asian vibe, our hosts discover that Quanzhou truly is a melting pot of world cultures. Then there’s the food: From the local noodle porridge that utilizes Silk Road spices, to fried vinegar pork and a dessert made from a special algae, there’s plenty of unique dishes to try here. Over a cup of oolong, our hosts will discover how Quanzhou’s tea changed the world, and how trade with Arab civilizations influenced a local fishing village. So join us in Quanzhou, a city that UNESCO designated as an “Emporium of the World”!

programme.title: Foodwise Quanzhou

programme.title: Foodwise: Xi'an
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Xi'an, an ancient city with over 3000 years of history, capital to 13 Chinese dynasties. But first, our hosts are going to carb load on street food, from glutinous rice cakes and cakes made out of persimmons, to mutton soup with flatbread and the famous biangbiang noodles. They'll also taste the rich history of Xi'an by experiencing a Qin Dynasty-inspired banquet, and try millennia-old dishes such as trout grilled on a ceramic tile and calabash chicken, a Tang Dynasty delicacy. From the Terracotta Army to the Daming Palace, residence of the Tang emperors, to a dazzling nighttime boulevard that recreates the grandeur of the Tang Dynasty, there's so much to explore in Xi'an. So, get your camera and your stomach ready for CGTN's Foodwise in Xi'an!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon - one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: My Little Cricket Fighter
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore a time-honored form of entertainment in China that has existed for thousands of years – cricket fighting. Music, Chinese chess, calligraphy and painting, and raising flowers, birds, fish and insects are known as the Eight Traditional Pastimes of the Chinese people. Raising insects may be the last on the list, but it is a pastime unique to China. Though these small creatures are tiny, the culture surrounding them has been nurtured by the Chinese people over thousands of years, embodying the unique cultural psychology, folk customs and aesthetic values of the Chinese nation.

programme.title: Shared Roots in Wrestling
programme.desc: The documentary “Shared Roots in Wrestling” follows a young wrestler from Tianjin as he journeys to Inner Mongolia to explore the shared heritage of Chinese-style wrestling and Bökh, the region’s national wrestling tradition. Part of CGTN’s original series “Next Stop: China,” this episode uncovers how strength, skill, and resilience connect athletes across city streets and endless grasslands, carrying forward a legacy that transcends geography and generations.

programme.title: In Search of Shunde Ep.3
programme.desc: A Bite of Shunde tells the stories of Shunde locals through food, showcasing this city’s heritage and present-day life. It looks at the craftsmanship Shunde people apply in the kitchen and beyond, and the dedicated, artisan mentality behind their renowned culinary culture. Through their attitude toward a simple home-cooked meal, we get insights into their values and way of life.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.5
programme.desc: Guangdong, sheltered by the Nanling Mountains, is a province where rivers cascade from hills on their way to the ocean. But before they meet the sea, they pass through another land of plenty, a place where solid earth encounters the rolling waves in a truly loving embrace - the Pearl River Delta.

programme.title: Into Guilin's landscapes: A new way to experience rural China
programme.desc: Guilin in south China's Guangxi region has long been celebrated for its breathtaking karst landscapes. Today, more and more travelers are discovering the region in a different way. Instead of simply admiring the scenery, they immerse themselves in it through cycling, hiking, bamboo rafting or via ferrata, experiencing the countryside from a new perspective. Supported by convenient transport links and a thriving outdoor recreation industry, Yangshuo County in Guilin is emerging as a global magnet where nature, culture and local life converge. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they explore Yangshuo through a variety of outdoor adventures.

programme.desc: Guilin in south China's Guangxi region has long been celebrated for its breathtaking karst landscapes. Today, more and more travelers are discovering the region in a different way. Instead of simply admiring the scenery, they immerse themselves in it through cycling, hiking, bamboo rafting or via ferrata, experiencing the countryside from a new perspective. Supported by convenient transport links and a thriving outdoor recreation industry, Yangshuo County in Guilin is emerging as a global magnet where nature, culture and local life converge. Join CGTN host Julian Waghann and Filipina singer Eliza Arce as they explore Yangshuo through a variety of outdoor adventures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Quanzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in Quanzhou, the ancient starting point of the Maritime Silk Road. From its covered arcades and Roman columns to its Southeast Asian vibe, our hosts discover that Quanzhou truly is a melting pot of world cultures. Then there’s the food: From the local noodle porridge that utilizes Silk Road spices, to fried vinegar pork and a dessert made from a special algae, there’s plenty of unique dishes to try here. Over a cup of oolong, our hosts will discover how Quanzhou’s tea changed the world, and how trade with Arab civilizations influenced a local fishing village. So join us in Quanzhou, a city that UNESCO designated as an “Emporium of the World”!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xi'an
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Xi'an, an ancient city with over 3000 years of history, capital to 13 Chinese dynasties. But first, our hosts are going to carb load on street food, from glutinous rice cakes and cakes made out of persimmons, to mutton soup with flatbread and the famous biangbiang noodles. They'll also taste the rich history of Xi'an by experiencing a Qin Dynasty-inspired banquet, and try millennia-old dishes such as trout grilled on a ceramic tile and calabash chicken, a Tang Dynasty delicacy. From the Terracotta Army to the Daming Palace, residence of the Tang emperors, to a dazzling nighttime boulevard that recreates the grandeur of the Tang Dynasty, there's so much to explore in Xi'an. So, get your camera and your stomach ready for CGTN's Foodwise in Xi'an!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. programme.title: My Little Cricket Fighter
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore a time-honored form of entertainment in China that has existed for thousands of years – cricket fighting. Music, Chinese chess, calligraphy and painting, and raising flowers, birds, fish and insects are known as the Eight Traditional Pastimes of the Chinese people. Raising insects may be the last on the list, but it is a pastime unique to China. Though these small creatures are tiny, the culture surrounding them has been nurtured by the Chinese people over thousands of years, embodying the unique cultural psychology, folk customs and aesthetic values of the Chinese nation.

programme.title: Shared Roots in Wrestling
programme.desc: The documentary “Shared Roots in Wrestling” follows a young wrestler from Tianjin as he journeys to Inner Mongolia to explore the shared heritage of Chinese-style wrestling and Bökh, the region’s national wrestling tradition. Part of CGTN’s original series “Next Stop: China,” this episode uncovers how strength, skill, and resilience connect athletes across city streets and endless grasslands, carrying forward a legacy that transcends geography and generations.

programme.title: In Search of Shunde Ep.3
programme.desc: A Bite of Shunde tells the stories of Shunde locals through food, showcasing this city’s heritage and present-day life. It looks at the craftsmanship Shunde people apply in the kitchen and beyond, and the dedicated, artisan mentality behind their renowned culinary culture. Through their attitude toward a simple home-cooked meal, we get insights into their values and way of life.

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu’s enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3
programme.desc: Join Tianran He on a high-speed train to Shigatse, gateway to the Himalayas and home to Mount Qomolangma, the world’s highest peak. As the city with the most land ports in Xizang, Shigatse serves as a key corridor to South Asia. Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: Inner Mongolia's Frozen Wonderland
programme.desc: In this episode, we feature the Winter Nadam Fair and winter sports in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia. By late December, the Hulunbuir Grassland is blanketed in ice and snow. Even in the bitter cold of around 30 degrees below zero, the grassland is alive with a festive bustle.

programme.desc: From China to France, America to India, and beyond - throughout human history, confectionery and desserts have united the world's shared sweet tooth, bringing hope and connection.

programme.desc: An exploration of authentic urban cuisine, this documentary unveils the hidden culinary world beneath the surface of Dongguan - an international city with a deeply rooted food culture.
